messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Pushed truncated normal distribution
parts:
Hey all,

I've pushed a truncated normal distribution.  I've actually had the code sitting in my local repository for a while but hadn't had a chance to clean it up.  I included (double based) unit tests but haven't included tests of the gradients.  It uses the regular normal_log implementation as its basis so it can benefit from most of the work that has been done there.  (That said, I haven't tested vectorization which would (probably) fail.)  Let me know if there are any issues that arise.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Pushed truncated normal distribution
parts:
Marcus's latest check in broke our build. (Marcus -- you
should subscribe the buildbot -- it sends out messages
when something breaks the build.)

I'm getting a problem in the definition of softmax
in math/special_functions, which at some point got
generalized to templated vectors and is at some point
being applied to Eigen vectors.

In file included from src/stan/agrad/special_functions.hpp:8:
src/stan/math/special_functions.hpp:362:29: error: no type named
'size_type' in 'Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var, -1, 1, 0, -1, 1>'
for (typename Vector::size_type i = 0; i < x.size(); ++i)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~

I don't understand where the error's coming from because
Daniel extended Eigen::Matrix with plugins so that it
implemented size_type. (For those who haven't been following
this, std::vector uses size_t and Eigen uses int for indices,
and if you don't use the right one, the compiler goes into
a hissy fit of warnings.)

The only way vectorization will work is if the code has
been explicitly vectorized the way that normal is. I'm
working right now on trying to extend the types to deal
with Eigen row and column vectors, too.

- Bob
